overview.text: The Mozdok image is a Caucasian form of the Iveron tradition. S.N.Savenko’s diocesan publication links its veneration with Ossetia, Queen Tamar and the later town of Mozdok.

blocks.text: The displayed image is a December 1895 chromolithograph preserved in the Saint George Church archive at Georgiyevsk. It shows the Mother of God and Child in a densely ornamented rectangular setting. The surviving print’s worn paper and darkened surface belong to that object. The 2022 upload date is not its artistic date, and this print is not relabelled the medieval shrine original.

blocks.text: Savenko recounts the tradition of Queen Tamar’s gift to Ossetian Christians and the icon’s movement with migrants from the Kurtatin gorge. The story explains its remaining at Mozdok through a sign during the journey. He records a church built in 1797 and later processions through Caucasian communities. These are a named historian’s account of local tradition and veneration, not proof of an uninterrupted medieval chain of custody for the displayed nineteenth-century print.

blocks.text: The publication reports the original’s disappearance during Soviet persecution and distinguishes later copies from it. It identifies Mid-Pentecost and the Dormition as observances. The movable feast and the printed15/28August pair are retained as the author’s calendar labels. The article’s healing testimonies remain attributed religious narratives rather than instructions for treating illness.
